title: Excitation spectra and rank tomography of linear matrix product tangent spaces
authors: Otto T. P. Schmidt, Iacopo Carusotto
abstract: We formulate a tangent-space method for algebraic varieties of matrix product states (MPS) to study excitation spectra of non-uniform quantum many-body systems with open boundary conditions. We further introduce a rank tomography of the MPS tangent space, which characterizes its expressivity in terms of particle-sector rank profiles of the underlying MPS variety. Using the Bose--Hubbard model as a benchmark, we illustrate that the method reproduces low-lying excitations and captures finite-size precursors of the Mott-insulator to superfluid transition.
summary: The paper introduces a sophisticated tangent-space method for analyzing excitation spectra in quantum many-body systems modeled by MPS. It enhances standard tensor network techniques by introducing 'rank tomography' to characterize state expressivity using particle-resolved rank profiles. This framework successfully applies to the Bose-Hubbard model, offering accurate spectral predictions while providing deep geometric insights into the underlying mathematical structure of the physical states.
main_problem: To develop a rigorous mathematical framework using tangent spaces to accurately calculate excitation spectra for quantum many-body systems described by Matrix Product States (MPS).
main_result: The method successfully reproduces low-lying excitations and captures finite-size precursors of the Mott-insulator to superfluid transition in the Bose-Hubbard model.
method: It employs a tangent-space approach on the algebraic variety defined by MPS, incorporating 'rank tomography' (PRSR) to characterize expressivity beyond simple bond dimensions. The dynamics are projected onto this variational tangent space using principles derived from time-dependent variational calculations.
model_or_system: The primary benchmark is the Bose-Hubbard model on an open chain of sites, analyzed within the MPS framework. The mathematical structure involves studying the geometry (smoothness) of the rank constraints defining the MPS variety.
key_observables: Excitation spectra ($\omega$), Particle-resolved Schmidt-rank distribution (PRSR), and the comparison between reconstructed vs. exact low-energy spectra.
important_parameters: Bond dimensions ($D$), coupling constants ($J$), interaction strength ($U$), chemical potential ($\mu$), and local Hilbert space dimension ($d$).
main_assumptions: The method provides a first-order approximation to excitations, and its applicability relies on the MPS representation being efficient for the Hamiltonian.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the MPS structure in gauge-fixed forms, compare exact vs. reconstructed low-energy spectra for the Bose-Hubbard model, and show the mathematical projection onto the tangent space.
paper_structure: The paper moves from defining the general tangent-space method on MPS varieties to applying it to the Bose-Hubbard model dynamics (TDVP). It also delves into the structural analysis of these varieties using rank tomography (PRSR) and algebraic geometry proofs regarding smoothness.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, mathematically rigorous extension of standard tensor network techniques (like DMRG/tDMRG) by incorporating differential geometric constraints to improve spectral accuracy and provide deeper insights into the underlying structure of quantum states.
